all.title: Launch-time preflight reroute of a device-approved direct task to a tool tool-capable provider
all.attack: After device approval, launch() preflight (revalidateCandidate) fails for the local route and calls rerouteFromDecision to pick a tool-capable fallback such as claude:null from the recorded fallback_order.
all.evidence: approve() adds the id to deviceApproved before launch (manager.server.ts:973). launch() reroutes via rerouteFromDecision at manager.server.ts:1077. Inside rerouteFromDecision the guard at lines 583-588 skips any entry with !next.model_id or !deviceMayLaunch(next), so claude:null and every non-ollama entry are skipped. A manual-mode task throws instead (launch around line 1073). The DEV-01 regression test in src/lib/bunny-host/remote-remediation.test.ts:418 covers the recovery path with an explicit local model. Blocked for this path.

all.title: Failure-recovery reroute (reroute and reroute-larger-context) of a device-approved task
all.attack: A device-approved local task fails with a taxonomy that triggers reroute or reroute-larger-context, and the recovery loop moves it to a cloud or tool-capable route.
all.evidence: Both recovery reroutes (manager.server.ts:1560) go through rerouteFromDecision, so the same guard at 583-588 applies. largerContext reorders the fallback via orderedByWindow but keeps the same filter. The loop's startSession (call sites around lines 1523, 1553, 1567) only accepts those targets. Test coverage: remote-remediation.test.ts:418. Blocked.

all.title: escalate-effort keeping the provider but switching model
all.attack: A verification failure on a device-approved task takes the escalate-effort branch and relaunches on a different model under the same provider, or falls through to a cloud route.
all.evidence: In the escalate-effort branch (around manager.server.ts:1534-1556), a raised effort produces target = {provider: current.provider, model: current.model, effort: raised}, so the model is unchanged. Only when raised is null (empty ladder) does it call rerouteFromDecision, which is guarded. Ollama's native effort ladder would need to be checked to confirm which branch fires; either way the model does not change. Blocked.

all.title: retry-same relaunch changing provider or model
all.attack: A retry-same action on a device-approved task relaunches with a different provider or model than the one approved.
all.evidence: retry-same (around manager.server.ts:1520-1530) calls startSession({provider: current.provider, model: current.model, effort: current.effort}) with the live record, so the target matches the current route. Blocked.

all.title: startSession invoked with a target not produced by rerouteFromDecision
all.attack: Find a startSession caller whose target is an arbitrary provider or model, bypassing the guard.
all.evidence: There are exactly three call sites: retry-same (same provider and model), escalate-effort (same model, or the rerouteFromDecision result), and reroute (rerouteFromDecision result only). startSession itself checks only eligibility, localOnly and mission scope, never the device set. The initial launch uses adapter.launch directly with the current record. Blocked: no caller can change provider or model outside rerouteFromDecision.

all.title: Ollama provider-default auto mapping to a cloud tag at launch
all.attack: A device-approved task with model auto is run on ollama, and execute() maps auto to probe.models[0], which may be a hosted cloud tag.
all.evidence: execute() at exec.server.ts:51-53 does const model = request.model || probe.models[0]; then requires probe.models.includes(model). The string auto is truthy, so it is never replaced by models[0]. It is not in the model list and is refused with Model auto is no longer available. Blocked for the auto string. Latent gap: a falsy model (empty string, null or undefined) would be replaced by probe.models[0], and deviceMayLaunch (device-authority.server.ts:29-30) returns true for an empty model because isRemoteOllamaTag({name:''}) is false. I could not find a current producer of an empty model: manager.server.ts:748-751 and router.ts:130 coalesce to auto. So the attack is not reachable with current code. Recommend rejecting falsy models in deviceMayLaunch.

all.title: deviceMayLaunch classifies remoteness by name only, so remote-metadata tags pass
all.attack: An installed ollama tag whose name lacks the -cloud or :cloud suffix but which Ollama reports as remote (remote_host or remote_model set) is device-approved and launched. Ollama then proxies generation to a hosted service, which violates the local tool-free contract. Reroutes to such a tag from a device-approved task are also allowed.
all.evidence: deviceMayLaunch (device-authority.server.ts:29-30) calls isRemoteOllamaTag({name: task.model}), so remote_host and remote_model are never seen. The Host's own classifier includes them (exec.server.ts:19-20). Probe data is kept in ProviderLive.remoteModels (adapters.server.ts:145) and used by runsLocally (router.ts:16-17, which also rejects anything in remoteModels), which the device guard ignores. All three callers pass name-only data: manager.server.ts:588, http.server.ts:565 (pending OrchTask) and missions manager.server.ts:1958. Whether Ollama ever returns a remote tag without the suffix is not verified offline. The DEV-01 test (remote-remediation.test.ts:418) only uses qwen3:8b with remote:[]. Fix: pass the provider's remoteModels or the probe remote flags into deviceMayLaunch.

all.title: Retarget of a device-approved task, or device-initiated retarget or feedback
all.attack: Change the provider or model of a device-approved task via retarget, either by a device or after a failed device launch leaves the task waiting.
all.evidence: retarget (manager.server.ts:869-871) requires state waiting_for_approval. A successful device approval moves the task to launching before adapter.launch (launch around 1029-1100). Only a launch that throws before the state change leaves the task waiting. Then the workstation can retarget, which is workstation authority. The id stays in deviceApproved, and a later device approval re-checks deviceMayLaunch on the new route (http.server.ts:565). DEVICE_RIGHTS (device-authority.server.ts:52-73) has no retarget, and assertDeviceAction (http.server.ts:464) refuses it. task.feedback only writes feedback on terminal tasks. Blocked.

all.title: Same task id approved twice (device then workstation, or workstation then device)
all.attack: Use a second approval to clear or re-set the device flag and change which reroute rules apply.
all.evidence: The set is keyed by task id, which is a crypto UUID. After a successful launch the state is not waiting_for_approval, so a second approve throws at manager.server.ts:1029. Before a failed launch, a workstation approve deletes the id (line 974), which is user-authority consent, and a later device approve re-adds it only after deviceMayLaunch passes. A device approve on a running task adds the id, which only narrows reroutes. Once added, the flag is never cleared by a device action. Blocked.

all.title: Relaunch after Host restart without the in-memory set
all.attack: After a restart the deviceApproved set is empty, so a previously device-approved task relaunches on a tool-capable route.
all.evidence: The constructor (around lines 131-151) marks launching, running, verifying, waiting_for_input and waiting_for_agent_approval tasks as failed and never relaunches anything. Only approve() (line 971) and approveDelegated (line 990) call launch(). approve() re-adds the id at line 973 before launch, so any post-restart launch re-enters the guard. Queued tasks are not auto-launched. Blocked. Note: the set is never pruned (memory-only growth), which is not a security issue.

all.title: Mission child launched via approveDelegated bypasses the device set
all.attack: A Mission child is launched through approveDelegated, which never adds to deviceApproved, so the DEV-01 reroute guard does not apply and the child can reroute to a tool-capable provider.
all.evidence: approveDelegated (manager.server.ts:990) calls launch() directly and never touches the set. Mission child reroutes are instead bounded by missionScopeCheck and missionAttemptAdmission, which enforce the envelope's providerScopeViolation (missions manager.server.ts:94-104 and 211). That is the accepted MA0R semantics: a phone-approved Mission envelope is exact authority, so provider scope comes from the envelope the device approved. Device-approved mission children answered through missions manager.server.ts:3285 are gated by deviceMayLaunch (line 1958) and are local only. The set is not consulted for mission children at all. Not a DEV-01 escape under the accepted design, but the guard covers direct tasks only.

all.title: Provider-reported model hook changing a device task's model after approval
all.attack: A provider reports a different model through the hooks.model callback, rewriting task.model after approval without rerouteFromDecision.
all.evidence: adapterHooks.model (manager.server.ts around 1205-1212) updates task.model via executor.model with no guard. The ollama adapter never calls hooks.model (adapters.server.ts:166-175 uses only event and output). Only parseAgentEvent (codex and claude normalizers, adapters.server.ts:182-184) calls it, and device-approved tasks are ollama only. Blocked for this path, but the callback is an unguarded model rewrite point if a non-ollama device route ever exists.

all.title: Time-of-check to time-of-use between the device HTTP check and manager.approve
all.attack: The task's route is changed between the deviceMayLaunch check (http.server.ts:565) and manager.approve, so the device launches a non-local route.
all.evidence: The approve case reads pending from db, checks deviceMayLaunch, and calls manager.approve(id, actor) (http.server.ts:570) with no await between them. The database and manager calls are synchronous, and manager.approve re-reads the task at launch. Blocked by single-threaded synchronous execution. This depends on keeping the handler synchronous; an await inserted between the check and the approve would reopen it.

verdicts.reasoning:
Not refuted. I found no code that blocks the path, and the cited lines match 0904132 exactly.

Confirmed in code:
- device-authority.server.ts:29-30: deviceMayLaunch checks only isRemoteOllamaTag({name: task.model}), so remote_host and remote_model are never read.
- exec.server.ts:19-20: the Host's own classifier treats remote_host/remote_model as remote. probeOllama (line 29) and model-capability.server.ts:191 (local: !remote.has(tag)) both use it, so the Host already records such a tag as non-local.
- router.ts:16-17: runsLocally also rejects anything in remoteModels, and the device guard ignores that.
- Name-only callers: http.server.ts:565 (direct approve), manager.server.ts:588 (reroute of device-approved tasks), missions manager.server.ts:1958.
- Nothing downstream closes the gap for device tasks. preLaunchRevalidate (routing.server.ts:316-337) checks listing and snapshot membership but not locality. manager.server.ts:1054 checks locality only when the task is localOnly/offlineOnly, and a device can omit those constraints.
- The default route is ollama current_model = models[0] (orch/router.ts:130, adapters.server.ts:145), which can be a remote-flagged tag. A device chat submit can therefore reach a remote tag, and approve then passes the name-only guard.

What keeps this at MEDIUM rather than higher: exploitation needs an installed Ollama tag that Ollama reports as remote (remote_host/remote_model set) but whose name lacks -cloud/:cloud. The repo does not show whether Ollama ever produces such a tag (e.g. via a Modelfile alias of a cloud model). That was not verified offline, so the precondition is unconfirmed, not disproven. The inconsistency with the Host's own classifier and runsLocally is real in code. The suggested fix (pass probe remote flags or provider.remoteModels into deviceMayLaunch) is sound.

Files: C:\Users\allam\Documents\new\bun-router\src\lib\bunny-host\device-authority.server.ts (lines 29-30), C:\Users\allam\Documents\new\bun-router\src\lib\orch\exec.server.ts (lines 19-29), C:\Users\allam\Documents\new\bun-router\src\lib\bunny-host\router.ts (lines 16-17), C:\Users\allam\Documents\new\bun-router\src\lib\bunny-host\routing.server.ts (lines 316-337), C:\Users\allam\Documents\new\bun-router\src\lib\bunny-host\manager.server.ts (lines 588, 1054). This review was read-only: no edits, no tests, no Host start.

Not refuted. The gap is real in the code as read (read-only, no edits or tests run).

Confirmed:
- src/lib/bunny-host/device-authority.server.ts:29-30 deviceMayLaunch passes only {name: task.model} to isRemoteOllamaTag, so remote_host and remote_model are never consulted.
- src/lib/orch/exec.server.ts:19-20 is the Host classifier that does check remote_host/remote_model. Probe output goes into ProviderLive.remoteModels (adapters.server.ts:145), which router.ts:16-17 runsLocally uses. The device guard ignores both.
- The repo's own fixture at src/lib/orch/exec.server.test.ts:34 treats {name:"some-hosted-model", remote_host:...} as remote. So the intended classifier covers unsuffixed remote tags, and the device guard disagrees with it.
- The device tests (src/lib/bunny-host/remote-device.test.ts:537-539) only exercise suffixed names, so nothing covers this case.
- exec.server.ts:42-67 execute() performs no remote check before POST /api/generate, so a remote-flagged tag runs hosted if launched.
- All three callers are name-only: manager.server.ts:588 (reroute), http.server.ts:565 (approve), missions manager.server.ts:1958 (Mission approval).

Searched for blocking code and found none:
- The launch-time locality check at manager.server.ts:1053 and 1257 is gated on task.constraints localOnly/offlineOnly, so it does not run for ordinary device-approved tasks.
- preLaunchRevalidate (routing.server.ts:316-337) checks eligibility and listing only, with no remote check.
- validateSubmit and the device submit path do not force localOnly.

Reachability: the device needs an installed tag with remote_host or remote_model set but no -cloud or :cloud suffix. A device cannot install models itself. Whether Ollama produces such a name in practice (for example via an ollama cp alias that keeps the remote manifest) was not verified offline, so the severity stays at MEDIUM and does not rise above it. Once such a tag exists, a device can reach it through a chat submit (which may carry modelOverride) followed by approve, or through a router-chosen fallback, and it launches hosted. The proposed fix (pass remoteModels or the probe remote flags into deviceMayLaunch) matches the gap.

all.title: Extended endDeviceGrants list (failed) lets Retry revive a device approval
all.attack: After a workstation revokes a device, the device-approved Mission is in state failed. Attack: workstation or any path calls mission.retry to re-arm it under the lost device's envelope.
all.evidence: http.server.ts:848 iterates missionsIn([...MISSION_ACTIVE,'failed']); line ~852 sets revokedAt on the envelope before any stop. manager.server.ts:3449-3453 retry() refuses when envelope is missing, revokedAt set, or expired, so the revoked envelope blocks Retry. The only other failed->ready edge is retry (machine.ts:12 allows failed->ready/planning/stopped; start only follows retry), and replan from failed also revokes (manager.server.ts:3512-3515). Blocked.

all.title: Revoke-then-stop covers waiting_for_user missions
all.attack: Device-approved Mission paused at waiting_for_user: revoke leaves admitted work running, or stop is skipped because the state is not active.
all.evidence: machine.ts:30 MISSION_ACTIVE = ready, running, waiting_for_user, verifying, so http.server.ts:856 calls missions.stop for waiting_for_user. manager.server.ts:3357-3443 stop() cancels children, ends batches, marks non-terminal steps stopped, resolves open requests as deny, releases the workspace and sets state stopped. Blocked; no stop gap for waiting_for_user.

all.title: Device approval landing between the revoke and the grant sweep
all.attack: A device request already in flight when the device is revoked calls mission.approve after the credential change but before endDeviceGrants lists missions, so the new envelope is missed by the sweep.
all.evidence: The /command handler re-runs authenticateDevice at dispatch (http.server.ts, 'Revalidate at dispatch') before any command runs. The revoke writes the credential change before endDeviceGrants (http.server.ts ~728-735). In the excerpt read, no await separates the dispatch revalidation from the synchronous missions.approve call, and the mission list is taken after the revoke. Device approvals that complete before revoke are therefore visible to the list. Blocked, with the caveat that the no-await property was checked only in the excerpt read.

all.title: Stale pre-await mission.state in the sweep can skip stop for a Mission a concurrent Retry just re-armed
all.attack: Device revoke sweep lists failed device-approved Missions A and B. While the loop awaits missions.stop(A) (which yields during child cancellation), the workstation calls mission.retry(B). B's envelope is still unrevoked, so retry succeeds and B moves to ready and running. The loop then reaches B with the stale state 'failed', revokes the envelope, and does not call stop because MISSION_ACTIVE.includes('failed') is false.
all.evidence: http.server.ts:848 iterates a materialized array (store.server.ts:105-107 returns Mission[] from .all()), so `mission.state` is the pre-await snapshot. http.server.ts:856 tests that stale value. manager.server.ts:3337 and 3381 await bus.cancel and cancelChildren, which yield. manager.server.ts:3444-3494 retry is synchronous and accepts a failed Mission whose envelope is not yet revoked. Result: B keeps running in-flight child work under a revoked envelope, the device.revoked event reports no unstopped Mission, and the stop the commit intends never happens. Fix: re-read missions.store.mission(mission.id).state before the active test, or stop any non-terminal Mission that has live steps. Not run; reasoned from code, and it requires a concurrent workstation Retry during the revoke.

all.title: unstopped counter conflates failures; a failed envelope revoke leaves Retry live with a misleading message
all.attack: (a) stop() throws 'already ended' or 'already in progress' for a Mission that finished or is being stopped concurrently, and the catch counts it as unstopped. (b) saveAuthorization throws before the revoke write, so the envelope stays live and failed Retry still works, yet the event says only that a Mission needs Stop.
all.evidence: http.server.ts:859-861 catch increments unstopped for any throw, including the saveAuthorization write at ~852-854. manager.server.ts:3357-3360 stop() throws 'Mission has already ended.' and 'Mission Stop is already in progress.'. The commit claims 'Retry cannot revive it', which does not hold in case (b). Impact is limited to reporting and to a store-write failure; no device path reaches it. Fix: separate revoke failure from stop failure and re-check state.

all.title: Agent Mission envelope survives the sweep; Retry re-arms it, but agentic admission still blocks
all.attack: A device re-consented an Agent Mission via reauthorizeAgent (provenance and grantedBy = device). The first loop revokes the agentic delegation to REVOKED but skips agents.stop when the profile is already stopped. The second loop skips agentic Missions, so the mission envelope stays unrevoked and a workstation Retry on a failed agentic Mission is allowed.
all.evidence: http.server.ts:834-839 sets REVOKED before the profile check. The second loop at 848-856 excludes missions.agentic.exists(mission.id). manager.server.ts:3449-3453 checks only the envelope. Blocked at admission: agenticIdentityViolation (manager.server.ts ~2160-2182) requires current_state === 'ACTIVE', and agenticProviderCheck (manager.server.ts ~1366-1368) routes provider launches through it. So no work starts. Residual: a stale envelope remains live, and the revoke is not uniform across Mission types.

all.title: Device approves a revised plan without naming planReference: replans is not incremented by plan() alone
all.attack: Revise the plan without replans going above 0, so an unbound device approve (no plan field) passes the F-03 check.
all.evidence: plan() is called only from create (manager.server.ts:564, replans starts at 0) and from replan() (manager.server.ts:3544, which increments replans at 3539). grep found no other plan() caller. commands.server.ts:50-51 maps mission.plan to missions.replan. So every revised plan has replans >= 1 and the check at manager.server.ts:724 fires. Blocked.

all.title: Host-internal or other step/scope mutation in waiting_for_approval without replan
all.attack: Change steps, requestedScope, root or providerConstraints while the Mission waits for approval, without incrementing replans, so a device approves a changed scope.
all.evidence: replaceSteps is called only from plan() (manager.server.ts:675). requestedScope is assigned only inside plan() (~687). configure() (manager.server.ts:297-325) changes only enabled, triggersEnabled, browserHeadless and limits, and the maxReplans limit bounds replans. The reroute providerConstraints write (~2910) runs only for running steps. The root is set only at create (manager.server.ts:531-532). Blocked.

all.title: Device-initiated replan or plan
all.attack: A paired device calls mission.replan or mission.plan to create a new plan that bumps replans, or to supply explicit steps.
all.evidence: commands.server.ts:27 REMOTE allow-list omits mission.plan, mission.replan and mission.create. The gate at the top of missionCommand throws WorkstationRequiredError for non-local access on any action outside REMOTE. Blocked.

all.title: Replay of a stale planReference after a replan
all.attack: Device reviewed plan P1 (replans=0), the workstation replans to P2 (replans=1), and the device approves with the old P1 reference, or with no reference.
all.evidence: manager.server.ts:717 refuses any planReference that differs from agenticPlanReference(id). agenticPlanReference (manager.server.ts:1686-1697) digests step ids, which replan regenerates with crypto.randomUUID (manager.server.ts:~568 ids map). So P1 and P2 never collide. manager.server.ts:724 refuses an unbound approve when replans > 0. Blocked.

all.title: Agentic Mission consent or re-consent path bypasses the revised-plan rule
all.attack: A device approves an Agent Mission, or re-consents it through reauthorizeAgent, after a replan.
all.evidence: deviceMissionRefusal (manager.server.ts ~1963-1966) refuses any mission for which agentic.exists or origin starts with 'agent:' before the replans check. reauthorizeAgent (manager.server.ts ~2063-2074) requires waiting_for_user, a WAITING_FOR_USER consent, and e.plan_reference === agenticPlanReference(missionId), so a replanned plan is refused. Blocked.

all.title: Is failed the only non-active non-terminal state that can reuse an envelope
all.attack: Find another non-active, non-terminal state (draft, planning, waiting_for_approval) that still holds a usable envelope.
all.evidence: machine.ts:3-15 transitions. authorizationId is set only in approve() with state ready (manager.server.ts:791) and by reauthorizeAgent (waiting_for_user). replan() revokes the envelope (manager.server.ts:3512-3515) and clears authorizationId (3536) before planning and waiting_for_approval. draft and planning have no envelope at all. So failed is the only such state. Blocked.

all.title: replan() awaits cancelChildren before revoking, so a concurrent Retry can re-arm the Mission mid-replan (pre-existing, not in 0904132)
all.attack: Replan on a failed or waiting_for_user Mission awaits cancelChildren while its envelope is still live. A concurrent mission.retry re-arms it to running. replan then revokes and calls plan(), which asserts running->planning and throws, leaving a running Mission with a revoked envelope and an incremented replans counter.
all.evidence: manager.server.ts:3511 await cancelChildren precedes the revoke at 3512-3515. retry (manager.server.ts:3444) accepts failed and waiting_for_user with a live envelope. plan() setMission asserts the transition (manager.server.ts ~405-412, assertMissionTransition on owned.state), and plan's first setMission is outside its try. Not verified by running; reasoned from code. Impact is a stuck-but-revoked Mission, not an authority gap.

all.title: Device self sign-out does not sweep device-approved envelopes (intentional, pre-existing)
all.attack: Device signs out with approvals outstanding, expecting its grants to end.
all.evidence: endDeviceGrants runs only when local is true (http.server.ts ~730: 'local ? await endDeviceGrants : {...zeros}'), per the comment 'never on self sign-out'. The device credential is revoked, so it cannot act. The envelopes remain for the workstation to stop or retry. This is unchanged by 0904132. Not a device capability; noted as a design observation, not a regression.

all.title: Workstation flows: regression check
all.attack: Check whether the F-03 narrowing, the endDeviceGrants change or the removed hostPathFree affect workstation approve, retry or the phone client.
all.evidence: The F-03 branch is gated by isDeviceActor (manager.server.ts:719-725), so workstation approve is unchanged. The phone client sends the plan field when it has planReference (src/store/use-island.ts:760-763), and remoteVerdicts attaches planReference only to waiting_for_approval Missions (manager.server.ts:2002-2005), so no client regression. The only workstation-visible change is that Retry on a device-revoked failed Mission is refused until a replan, which is intended. The sign-out return default adds unstopped:0 consistently. No regression found.

verdicts.reasoning:
Could not refute the race. The code path is concrete and matches the finding.

Confirmed:
- missions.store.missionsIn (src/lib/bunny-missions/store.server.ts:105-107) returns a materialized Mission[] from .all(), so mission.state in the sweep loop (src/lib/bunny-host/http.server.ts:848-856) is a pre-await snapshot.
- Within the loop, stop(A) is awaited. stop() (src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:3357) awaits cancelChildren, and that awaits bus.cancel and tasks.stop. tasks.stop (src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1676) does real process inspection I/O when a session pid exists, so a macrotask yield is possible and an HTTP retry can interleave. Nothing serializes the device.revoke handler against other requests.
- retry() (manager.server.ts:3444-3494) is workstation-only (commands.server.ts: mission.retry is not in REMOTE). It accepts a failed Mission whose envelope is unrevoked and unexpired, sets it to ready, and calls start(). start() (manager.server.ts:799-810) has no active-count limit (that check is only in approve() at line 736), so retry succeeds and B becomes running.
- At B, the loop re-reads the envelope fresh and revokes it, but the stale state "failed" is not in MISSION_ACTIVE, so stop(B) is skipped while B is running.

Narrowing points (these do not refute it):
- The attack text lists A as failed. A failed A would never get stop() called, so the trigger needs A to be running at snapshot time. The defect still holds with that correction.
- The race needs stop(A) to actually yield. If A has no live child I/O, the await chain stays in microtasks and no retry can interleave.
